title: Map & Locations
imageAlt: Stylized map preview for Omni locations
summary: A reference for major known locations, including the hospital, The Camp, and later story areas.
intro: Locations in Omni feel ordinary at first, then reveal that ordinary life has been interrupted, copied, or preserved in the wrong way.

details.label: Exploration style
details.value: Quiet routes, clue sites, returning locations

facts: The world looks left behind rather than destroyed.
No-service areas and broken signals are recurring clues.
Several locations are revisited after The Camp gives the player tools or context.

sections.heading: Hospital
paragraphs: The Hospital is the first known location and the site where the player wakes from a coma. It appears abandoned, mostly intact, and recently emptied.
Early exploration focuses on locked doors, dead monitors, unanswered phones, empty staff stations, and signs that the player was not treated like a normal patient.
A later return reveals restricted records, observation rooms, and evidence that the hospital staff knew about almost-human visitors before the player woke up.
items: Type: opening area, later investigation site.
Connected story beat: the player's survival and missing time.
Clue: patient files marked with Omni-related terminology.

sections.heading: Overgrown Town
paragraphs: The Overgrown Town surrounds the hospital. It includes empty roads, abandoned vehicles, closed shops, houses with untouched interiors, and plants growing through maintained spaces.
This area gives the player their first look at the larger world. It is quiet enough that every sign of movement feels important.
The town can expand in stages after The Camp, with new routes opening for supply runs, signal checks, and hospital return objectives.
items: Type: early exploration zone.
Connected story beat: first realization that the emptiness is larger than the hospital.
Clue: emergency notices that use careful wording instead of naming the threat.

sections.heading: The Camp
paragraphs: The Camp is the main hub and the first place that contains an organized group. It is introduced through Ali and becomes the player's base after the first encounters.

It contains practical stations for supplies, planning, repairs, and signal work. It also contains social unease: repeated routines, avoided topics, and residents who appear human but do not fully behave like it.
The Camp changes as the story progresses. The more the player learns, the more defensive or unstable the camp's normal behavior becomes.
items: Type: hub, social mystery location.
Connected story beat: trust becomes complicated.
Clue: camp rules that make more sense after learning about Omni.

sections.heading: No-Service Zones
paragraphs: No-Service Zones are areas where phones, radios, and emergency signals fail completely or behave strangely. They help make the lack of communication feel like part of the lore.
Some zones are silent, while others play fragments of old broadcasts or repeated phrases. Signal behavior becomes a way to track Omni's influence.
Amy is tied to these zones through her interest in patterns, while Ali discourages the player from investigating them too closely.
items: Type: recurring environmental condition.
Connected story beat: the world is being blocked or filtered.
Clue: a broadcast using a camp resident's voice before the player has heard them say it.

sections.heading: Signal Tower
paragraphs: The Signal Tower is a midgame objective. The player reaches or repairs it hoping to contact the outside world.
Instead of restoring normal service, the tower reveals corrupted local transmissions. These include hospital audio, copied voices, and phrases that sound like they were assembled from human memories.
The tower marks the point where the player can no longer treat the empty world as a simple disaster.
items: Type: midgame investigation site.
Connected story beat: Omni becomes an active force.
Clue: a transmission that reacts to the player's presence.

sections.heading: Outer Roads
paragraphs: The Outer Roads lead away from the main town and toward checkpoints, blocked exits, old supply caches, and later story locations.
They make the world feel larger while still refusing the player a clean escape. Roads loop, collapse, or lead to places that suggest other groups tried to leave and failed.
Ali knows these routes too well. Amy knows which ones still carry signal traces.
items: Type: expanded traversal area.
Connected story beat: the emptiness is not local.
Clue: signs of organized evacuation without evidence of arrival.

sections.heading: Other Camp
paragraphs: The Other Camp is a late-midgame location. It is a failed settlement, duplicate camp, or abandoned testing ground that mirrors the player's own hub.
This location reveals that The Camp is part of a wider pattern. The player finds similar rules, repeated station layouts, and names connected to current camp residents.
It stands as a warning. Whatever is happening at the player's camp has happened before, and it did not end cleanly.
items: Type: late-midgame reveal location.
Connected story beat: The Camp is not unique.
Clue: a camp rule list matching the player's camp word for word.
